prompt: What physical quantity is represented by the gradient of a velocity-time graph?

answer.explanation: The gradient of a velocity-time graph is Delta v / Delta t, which represents the rate of change of velocity, defining acceleration.

distractor_explanations: Correct: gradient = Delta v / Delta t = acceleration.
Displacement is represented by the area under a velocity-time graph, not the gradient.
Force requires mass (F = ma) and is not directly given by the gradient alone.
Velocity is the value read directly from the vertical axis, not the gradient.
hints: The vertical axis is velocity in m s^-1 and horizontal axis is time in s.
Rate of change of velocity gives acceleration.
solution: A. Gradient = Delta v / Delta t = acceleration.
teacher_walkthrough: On a velocity-time graph, gradient = Delta v / Delta t.
Rate of change of velocity is the definition of acceleration.
The units confirm this: (m s^-1) / s = m s^-2. Option 1 is correct.
